issues.title: [Plan Review §contracts] ipc.dispatch return-slice lifetime vs WebKit JSC string con…
issues.description:
## Finding (severity: critical)
ipc.dispatch return-slice lifetime vs WebKit JSC string construction is unspecified. `dispatch` returns `[]const u8` allocated in an arena. The C shim must then construct a JSCValue (via jsc_value_new_string or equivalent) and call webkit_script_message_reply_return_value. The contract does not specify whether jsc_value_new_string copies the bytes before the arena is freed, nor who frees the arena and when. A wrong ordering produces a use-after-free that silently corrupts the IPC reply or crashes the process.

## Where in the plan
/home/maceo/ntm_Dev/zigBrowser/thoughts/searchable/shared/plans/2026-05-31-14-41-ENG-0004-tdd-webkitgtk-appshell-slice2.md  §C12 — IPC bridge contract (the differentiator, minimal)  ~line 184
```
- C reads the message via `webkit_javascript_result_get_js_value` → `JSCValue` → `jsc_value_to_string`
  (javascriptcoregtk-4.1, linked in Slice 1), parses the JSON envelope, and calls Zig:
  ```zig
  // src/ipc.zig — pure dispatch, unit-testable
  pub const IpcError = error{ UnknownCommand, BadArgs };
  pub fn dispatch(arena, cmd: []const u8, args_json: []const u8) IpcError![]const u8; // returns JSON
  ```
- Minimal command set (all return values JS cannot fabricate on its own — independent oracle):
```

## Impact
Unspecified memory ownership at the Zig→C→WebKit boundary makes every IPC reply unsafe by default. Any implementation that frees the arena before jsc_value_new_string copies the string produces a use-after-free with no compile-time signal, directly breaking the 'js-calls-zig-and-sees-result' differentiator behavior.

## Recommendation
Document the mandatory ordering with an inline comment in webkit_shim.c's IPC callback: (1) call zb_ipc_dispatch into a local buffer or arena; (2) immediately call jsc_value_new_string — which copies the bytes; (3) free the arena/buffer; (4) call webkit_script_message_reply_return_value with the now-owned JSCValue. No library change needed; a one-line comment pins the contract.
